F0.rationale: Baseline hygiene remains PM-owned and presence-only; ghostmux has most floor surfaces but no repo-declared secret-scan hook.

P0.rationale: ghostmux mutates real terminal state; the precondition is a runnable local verify gate enforced by committed hooks.

S1.rationale: The repo already has typed API models and a shared surface resolver; high-risk command options and metadata payloads are still parsed as raw strings/dictionaries.

S1.authorityChannelSplit.rationale: ghostmux does not compile launch/runtime authority overlays; probe only if it starts dispatching compiled runtime artifacts.

S2.rationale: Twenty command structs follow a dominant protocol, but new command work still depends on manual registration and duplicated help/docs updates.

S3.rationale: Agents enter through AGENTS.md and route into Justfile, README, docs, and tests; command disclosure is checked against live command tokens.

S3.affordanceGating.rationale: ghostmux is a Swift CLI/library package and does not assemble model prompts or dynamically project tool/skill carrier surfaces.

S4.rationale: The CLI controls real terminals over a UDS protocol; boundary and discovery guards need diagnostics that tell an agent what to fix.

S5.rationale: Smoke skips, hook bypasses, and formatter disables must be visible and issue-backed because they can silence the local gate.

S6.rationale: The hook-enforced verify loop exists; it still needs to include the repo’s unit/contract test carriers or intentionally retire them.

S7.rationale: Command tokens are now guarded, but README options/examples and some runbook carriers can still drift silently.

S7.contractHashClosure.rationale: No compiled cross-process contract artifact is produced by ghostmux itself; keep as a frontier sighting only if generated launch/session artifacts land here.

S8.rationale: Broad Swift style and taste rules should remain judgment; ghostmux should mechanize only repeated, concrete failures with negative-smoke evidence.

TA.rationale: Praesidium can supply architect/builder/smoke roles, but ghostmux does not own a repo-local role-separation gate.

TA.actuatorSplit.rationale: Credential-separated actuation is upstream platform policy, not currently a ghostmux repo mechanism.

TB.rationale: AGENTS.md now carries closeout procedure; there is still no invokable repo-local skill.

TB.lifecycleHealth.rationale: ghostmux does not let agents create or mutate skills inside the repo.

TC.rationale: AGENT_ENABLEMENT_RETRO.md exists and has one remediation closeout entry; no cadence trigger is enforced.

TD.rationale: Agents use ghostmux as a terminal actuator; command discovery must derive from the live dispatch registry, not stale prose.

TD.selfDescribingSurfaceConformance.rationale: Command-token conformance is present, but README option/example drift remains observable at HEAD.

TE.rationale: A real Ghostty smoke is the required acceptance proof for terminal behavior and now fails closed under just verify.

TE.claimScopedEvidenceRouting.rationale: Smoke result states are useful claim evidence, but full proof-profile routing remains frontier and should not gate ghostmux today.

TE.crossHarnessConformanceMatrix.rationale: ghostmux has one ScriptableGhostty UDS harness, not interchangeable providers.

TF.rationale: ghostmux is a terminal actuator and ghostchat metadata tool, not the executable work-state control plane; work transitions belong upstream in wrkq/hrc.

TF.workflowAdoption.rationale: No ghostmux-owned work-state engine exists to adopt; do not count terminal lifecycle state as a TF work-control plane.
